text: Let us delve deeper into theoretical physics.
What happens to the invisible fabric of gravity itself when time stops?
According to Albert Einstein's General Theory of Relativity, space and time are not separate entities.
They are woven together into a unified four-dimensional fabric called spacetime.
Gravity is not a mysterious invisible tractor beam; it is the physical curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
Furthermore, modern physics has proven that changes in gravitational fields propagate through space at exactly the speed of light—carried by gravitational waves.
If time ceases to flow, does the Earth continue to pull you downward?
If gravitational waves are frozen in transit, the gravitational force field around you becomes completely static.
If you jump or attempt to push off any surface, you would remain suspended indefinitely in zero-gravity drift, floating helplessly in the dark.
Conversely, if spacetime curvature freezes without the temporal dimension, the mathematical equations governing general relativity break down into infinite mathematical singularities.
In attempting to freeze time, you have severed the fundamental metric tensor that holds physical reality together.
